description: Semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations provide systematic upper bounds for combinatorial optimization problems. The LCS problem can be formulated as an integer program over binary alignment matrices. An SDP relaxation yields a provable upper bound on E[LCS], potentially tighter than existing automata-based upper bounds.
mathematical_formalization: Let A_{ij} in {0,1} indicate position i in x matched to j in y. LCS = max sum A_{ij} subject to: A_{ij}=0 if x_i != y_j, monotonicity. Relax to A in [0,1], add PSD constraint A >= 0 plus Lasserre hierarchy. SDP value averaged over random (x,y) upper bounds gamma_2 * n.
analogical_connections: Lovasz theta function for graph capacity
implementation_hypothesis: Formulate LCS IP for fixed n. Write first-level Lasserre relaxation. For small n (5-10), solve SDP exactly. Average over all string pairs.
experiment_seed: Implement LCS as IP for n=5. Write Lasserre-1 SDP relaxation. Solve for all 2^10 string pairs. Average. Ratio gives upper bound candidate.
